headline: High: ctx can observe Claude Code events while dexter has broad network egress, creating dangerous default pathways for prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and touches filesystem/logs, so it can ingest agent-produced content; dexter has autonomous execution and broad network egress, making externally sourced content plausible. The shared bridge is indirect, not proven by a documented shared channel, so medium is the higher defensible severity.
conditions: IF ctx reads dexter-generated text from a shared workspace or log file, injection becomes actionable.
IF dexter forwards web content into ctx-observed events, ctx may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions.
mitigations: Restrict ctx to a read-only view of dexter outputs.
Add a provenance tag to all dexter-generated files.
Disable automatic instruction-following on observed event text.
Review any shared filesystem path before enabling both agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between dexter outputs and ctx inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, harness records, graph data, and filesystem; dexter touches financial and market data and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/. A shared workspace is not explicitly documented, but if one exists, sensitive data could flow between them and into dexter's API calls or ctx logs.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory, data leakage risk is present.
IF dexter uploads scratchpad contents to external APIs, any ctx-written sensitive logs can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Keep sensitive files out of .dexter/scratchpad/.
Disable or redact ctx runtime logging for shared runs.
Use per-agent credentials and API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and run browsers, while dexter has autonomous execution with broad network egress and multiple API integrations. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes or API-side state changes can collide if they share resources; locking is not documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path, write conflicts can occur.
IF both agents use the same external API credentials, mutable remote state can collide.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use separate API keys per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent browser sessions against the same account.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe tool events, so its outputs can become authoritative context for dexter's autonomous execution. dexter can then act over networked APIs without a built-in verification step in the profile, creating a default pathway where one agent's mistaken output can trigger downstream actions or bad trades.
conditions: IF dexter consumes ctx-generated summaries as facts, errors can cascade into external actions.
IF ctx records stale or partial tool events, dexter may act on incorrect state.
mitigations: Require human review before dexter acts on ctx-derived outputs.
Mark ctx outputs as untrusted by default.
Add a verification step before any external API call.
Limit dexter to read-only mode for shared runs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while dexter handles financial and market data and sends it to third-party APIs. The pair creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated financial data is logged or forwarded, though no specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is written into ctx logs, retention policy mismatch may occur.
IF dexter forwards market or financial data to external APIs without a DPA, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared logs.
Review API vendor terms before enabling both agents.
Set short log retention on ctx outputs.
Use a data-classification checklist for financial inputs.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data.
